subject: science
title: Protect Our Earth
about: Ways people protect natural resources: recycle, reuse, reduce, compost, save water and power, replant trees, no litter (ESS.1.3.2). NC wants children to argue for these from evidence; the cards give them the facts to argue with.
tip: Let him be the recycling boss for a week: he decides what goes in the bin and says why.

cards.q: You finish a box of cereal. What should you do with the empty box?
cards.note: Old boxes can be made into new paper.

cards.q: You have a bag from the store. How can you reuse it?
cards.note: Using a bag again means one less new bag.

cards.q: You want to reduce trash. What can you do?
cards.note: Less stuff used means less trash made.

cards.q: People cut down trees for wood. What should they do after?
cards.note: New trees grow up to take the place of the old ones.

cards.q: You leave a room. What do you do to save power?
cards.note: Lights that are off use no power.

cards.q: What can you make from food scraps and leaves?
cards.note: Compost turns scraps into rich soil.

cards.q: Which one goes in the recycling bin?
cards.note: Paper, plastic, metal and glass can be recycled.

cards.q: A hose is running and nobody is using it. What do you do?
cards.note: That is one way to conserve water.

cards.q: You brush your teeth. How do you save water?
cards.note: Turn the water on only to rinse.
If we waste it, we could run short.

cards.q: You have a candy wrapper outside. Where does it go?
cards.note: Trash in a can is not litter.

cards.q: What can litter in a pond hurt?
cards.note: A clean pond is a safe home for the animals in it.

cards.q: You draw on paper. How can you save trees?
cards.note: Using both sides of a sheet means fewer trees cut.

cards.q: What does riding a bike instead of a car save?
cards.note: A car burns fuel. A bike just needs your legs.

cards.q: What does a shorter shower save?
cards.note: Every minute in the shower uses more water.
